label: S. 2403
title: Retire through Ownership Act
summary: Retire through Ownership Act This act allows the fiduciary of an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) to rely on a valuation provided by an independent valuation expert or business appraiser in determining the fair market value of the plan's assets if the assets are not securities for which there is a generally recognized market and the expert or appraiser follows specified methodologies. In general, ESOPs are defined contribution pension plans where employees accrue shares of their employers' stock in individual accounts as part of their compensation. After separating from employment or retiring, employees receive the cash value of their shares. Under the act, an independent expert or appraiser must adhere to the methodology established under the Internal Revenue Service Ruling 59-60, which prescribes the factors a professional business appraiser should consider in forming a valuation of the stock for a closely held business.
summary_short: Lets the manager of an employee stock ownership plan rely on an independent appraiser’s value for company stock that is not publicly traded, as long as the appraisal follows set IRS methods.
summary_source: Solon Watch, based on the Congressional Research Service summary
